value.body: A medical officer is a doctor in a salaried post who sees patients, handles emergencies and runs health programmes. State health departments, central government health services, hospitals, the armed forces, railways and companies hire them. A day may include outpatient clinics, ward rounds, emergency duty and public-health work.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: MBBS with internship and medical registration

items.label: Primary Health Centres
items.note: Government PHCs, each usually staffed by medical officers

value.title: How you get in
value.body: After MBBS and the compulsory internship, doctors register with the National Medical Commission or a State Medical Council. Government posts are filled through state public service commission or health-department recruitment, and the UPSC Combined Medical Services exam for central services. Private hospitals recruit directly.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Running national health programmes and records
Working with nurses and paramedical staff

value.title: At a glance
items: Rural service may be required or rewarded in some states, for example through bonds or PG entrance weightage.
Many medical officers prepare for PG entrance exams alongside the job.
Common next steps: a specialist degree (MD/MS/DNB) or senior medical officer posts in government service.

competition.note: MBBS graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
